items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: He couldn't take it away from him. He was sort of a military band. He had a good band.

ctx.x: I mean Manuel had a good band.

He couldn't take it away from him. He was sort of a military band. He had a good band. Now there's only one band in this town that plays almost. Well, in fact, if you sit up, heard my band play and walk away and hear this colored band play, you'd hear my same stuff. What's his name? Paul Barbarian. Who? Barbarian. Barbarian. Barbarian. I guess that is. Barbarian. Barbarian. The same kind of stuff and almost the same temperature. They've got two, they've got two of those color bands as the same.
They both played for the Jazz at their auditorium one night. What's that other name of that other colored band?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: Perez? That's it. That's it. He had a band. He was a leader, too.

ctx.x: Yeah. Paul Morat, no, no, no. Perez? That's it. That's it. He had a band. He was a leader, too. He had a band. This fella, I can't think of his name right now. It's right on my memory, too, his name. It's on the tip of my tongue. It'll come to you. You'll think of it when we leave. Yeah, I'll think of it. Well, he had a band, and, in fact, after he started, there were two or three bands started. It was a fella by the name, as I told you, Green. A fella by the name of Green started a band. He started a band when…
Do you know Tom Ehrle? I guess you must know.
